description:
## Goal

Remove avoidable ordinary Fz/CPS wrapper calls with one small general inlining rule. Preserve source callable identity, evaluation order, exact result lanes, effects, and failure behavior. This is a later optimization after truthful externs and physical ABI validation, not a prerequisite for arithmetic correctness.

## Starting contract

fz-5xp.30 supplies private truthful runtime extern declarations, total C arithmetic exports, and unboxed {value, boolean} return lanes. Interpreter, JIT, and AOT make ordinary calls to those real C exports. Kernel routes arithmetic status through its private generic arithmetic_result/1 helper and arithmetic_error/0, currently panic(:badarith). There is no arithmetic-specific native substitution, intrinsic syntax, source-name whitelist, special Kernel dispatch, or fake foreign export.

A foreign call inside an operator does not eliminate the caller to Kernel.+/2 or the ordinary helper call. This ticket owns only general direct Fz-call overhead. It does not excuse an FFI, boxing, ABI, or semantic regression in .30.

## Strategy

1. Inspect current backend call/return delivery, existing optimization patterns, retained product boundaries, and exact ordinary call counts.
2. Define one bounded structural eligibility class for resolved direct Fz bodies. It must cover a one-call wrapper and the current checked arithmetic path: call real extern, bind its {result, failed} lanes, then return result or enter the existing failure helper. The rule must not depend on a source function name, module, or foreign symbol.
3. Reuse the typed body and control representation. Substitute already-evaluated arguments once; preserve order, selected overload, source locations, result/status correlation, effects, and the error path. Do not materialize/deconstruct a tuple, clone bodies speculatively across a root, or inspect a C body.
4. Dynamic calls, recursion, code-size limits, and every ineligible shape keep the ordinary call path. Source function identity remains for captures and first-class uses even when a selected direct call inlines.
5. Measure reductions in calls, bodies, code bytes, evaluations, and exact causal work. Unchanged requests must retain existing products; unrelated edits must not expand an inline cone.

## Acceptance

- RED tests count the avoidable direct Fz call before the change and prove its removal for a plain wrapper, the current status-pair helper shape, and a user-defined structurally equivalent wrapper.
- Interpreter/JIT/AOT semantics and failures match; effects run once in order. Inlining preserves scalar lanes, does not create arithmetic boxing, and retains the real-call and cold-error behavior. Tests force ordinary fallback where ineligible.
- Eligibility is structural and typed, not spelling-based. No private optimizer mini-compiler, global rescan, duplicate cache, deep clone on unchanged demand, or uncontrolled code growth.
- Delete any bespoke wrapper shortcut only when the one general mechanism replaces it. Reuse predecessor ABI/arithmetic fixtures instead of duplicating compiler work.
- Update pipeline/optimization and extern docs with exact eligibility/fallback. Focused and full gates pass; fresh cold Sol-high scoped review; one commit/close and prompt gh-stack push.

## Order and boundaries

Blocked by fz-5xp.32, which is blocked by .30. Proper language exceptions are independent work in fz-kdt.28; this ticket preserves the actual current helper endpoint without depending on panic versus raising.

General loop/vector optimization, range-based arithmetic-check removal, larger foreign aggregates, and cross-language C inlining are out of scope. Before construction, present verified facts and a bounded strategy to the user. Do not use Astra without explicit permission.
title: Inline small ordinary Fz wrappers while preserving foreign calls and failure branches
